lines.text: Two of my projects are the same idea, twice.
In Pulsemind, an XGBoost classifier scores every reading from an ICU stream.
In the demo, scoring a reading and explaining it takes about forty-three milliseconds.
Only when it flags an anomaly does the system pay for a language model.
In Develarper, a small local model reads each task's difficulty first.
On the team's routing evaluation, it sent seven hundred and eleven of eight hundred tasks to the right tier.
Hard tasks go to the cloud. The rest stay on the local model.
The expensive step runs only when the cheap one asks for it.
